subject: CloudWave AWS listing — annual vs consumption pricing & procurement signoff

Subject: CloudWave AWS listing — annual vs consumption pricing & procurement signoff

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I promised to send a concise view of the two pricing paths we're seeing for listings on AWS Marketplace and the approval implications for each. Attached: CloudWave_MPO_term_matrix.xlsx (matrix with 3 scenarios).

High-level options we recommend:
- Annual committed (12 months): lowest unit price; requires finance/CFO review for multi-year commitments and a standard procurement PO; target procurement path: Procurement -> Finance -> Legal (if SOW/terms custom) -> CFO for >$250k.
- Consumption (pay-as-you-go): higher per-unit, faster activation; procurement signoff typically only needs Procurement + Tech buyer; preferred if buyer wants short runway or pilot.
- Hybrid (6-month pilot with conversion credit): pilot priced as consumption with a conversion credit toward a 12-month commit if activated within the pilot window.

Key asks for CloudWave to move to final quote:
1) Confirm which pricing path you want (annual / consumption / hybrid).
2) Share the buyer/approver list and estimated internal signoff SLA (days to approval).
3) Any procurement clauses we should pre-bake (PO wording, invoicing cadence).

We can support a DocuSign flow and provide a stripped-down evidence pack for procurement if that helps speed approvals. Vanessa and Olga are cc'd to chime in on approval thresholds and the quote.

Best,
David

--
David Kim

Subject: Re: CloudWave AWS listing — annual vs consumption pricing & procurement signoff

Thanks David — useful framing. A couple quick clarifications before we escalate internally.

1) Approval chain: for purchases that will be billed via Marketplace private offer we need: Procurement -> Finance (budget hold) -> Security (light review) -> Legal only if there are contract deviations. CFO only signs for >$300k ARR (our internal threshold). Can you confirm whether Redwood recommends Legal review for the annual template or if the AWS listing + MPO quote is usually sufficient?

2) Term: Our product team wants to trial a 6-month pilot, but Finance prefers 12-month to get better unit pricing. Is there a standard conversion credit you typically include if a pilot converts to annual?

3) PO specifics: we require net-45 payment terms on POs. Will that be acceptable for a Marketplace-backed invoice flow? Procurement copied — pls advise.

Also can you re-run the matrix with list pricing vs committed pricing at the 100k token/month footprint (we want the cost delta). If it's easier, Vanessa/Olga feel free to share a quick note on whether a 6-month pilot is feasible from Redwood's activation standpoint.

Thanks,
Sarah

--

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: CloudWave AWS listing — procurement/approval notes and quote

Forwarding internal — I pulled together the procurement thresholds and our suggested activation play. David, feel free to paste to CloudWave.

Internal notes (short):
- Legal typically not required for standard MPO flows where customer accepts AWS Marketplace terms and the MPO quote contains the price/term. We recommend Legal review only if CloudWave adds custom SOW language or requires data residency clauses.
- For a 6-month pilot -> 12-month conversion, our usual structure is: pilot on consumption pricing with a one-time conversion credit equal to 15% of pilot spend applied to first 3 months of the annual commit. We can flex this % for enterprise deals.
- PO/payment: Marketplace invoicing generally supports net-45 via the buyer's invoicing setup, but we need Procurement to confirm they can accept Marketplace invoices vs buyer-managed invoicing. If not, we can issue invoice via Redwood and map to the MPO activation; this will need Finance approval.

Attached: redwood_mpo_quote_v2.pdf (includes two pricing rows and DocuSign-ready text).

Suggested next steps to propose to CloudWave:
1) Approver list (Procurement, Finance lead, Security reviewer) + expected SLA (days).
2) Accept pilot structure above or request a specific conversion %.
3) Confirm preferred invoicing path (Marketplace invoice vs vendor invoice).
4) Sign via DocuSign link (I can prepare).

Vanessa

Sarah / Procurement team — thanks for the quick answers. Summarizing an agreed path so we have a mutual action plan: 

1) Pricing & term
- CloudWave to commit to a 6-month pilot on consumption pricing with a conversion credit of 15% of pilot spend if you convert to the 12-month annual commit within the pilot window. (If you prefer a different credit we can negotiate.)

2) Approvals & timeline
- Approvers: Procurement (procurement@cloudwave.com) -> Finance (budget approval) -> Security (brief checklist review) -> Legal only if CloudWave requests contract modifications.
- Please confirm names & target SLA (we usually see 7–21 business days depending on Finance availability).

3) PO & invoicing
- We can support Marketplace invoicing on net-45. If Procurement cannot accept Marketplace invoices, Redwood can issue a vendor invoice mapped to MPO activation (this will add a short finance approval step).

4) Attachments & next actions
- Attached: CloudWave_MPO_term_matrix.xlsx (updated columns), redwood_mpo_quote_v2.pdf (DocuSign-ready).
- DocuSign link for quote: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abcd-efgh-2026

Action items for CloudWave:
- Confirm pilot acceptance and list of approvers + SLA by EOD Friday (20 Nov).
- Procurement to confirm invoicing preference.

If you prefer, Vanessa will send the DocuSign envelope and I can set the MPO in AWS once we receive the signed quote.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to activation.

Best,
David
